# Selecting a toolchain

cpp-anything's default target is C++23 on GCC 13: the oldest release in the matrix with `-std=c++23`, complete C++20 core support and a libstdc++ that has `std::expected`. This page explains the default and lists the alternatives.

Matrix: 651 features, generated 2026-11-19T12:57:02+00:00, from cppreference (cppreference.com compiler support tables (CC-BY-SA 4.0 / GFDL)).
Refresh the data with `cpp-anything matrix sync` (or `scripts/sync_matrix.py`), then

## The default, and why

`bridge` writes `--toolchain gcc --version 13 --std c++23` unless told otherwise:

- C++23 is the policy cpp-anything's generated code is written for: `[[nodiscard]]`, `std::string_view`, `std::span`, ranges and `std::expected` everywhere.
- The wire format needs a value-or-error type. On C++23 targets that is `std::expected`; on C++20 targets the generated header defines `cppan::Result<T>` with the same interface, so the same port source compiles for either standard.
- GCC 13 is the default because it is the oldest release with `-std=c++23`, complete C++20 core support and a libstdc++ that has `std::expected`; a newer GCC closes the C++23 gaps listed in [compilers/gcc.md](compilers/gcc.md).

## Minimum release per target, from the matrix

| standard | toolchain | core complete | library complete |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c++20 | GCC | 12 | 14 |
| c++20 | Clang/libc++ | — | — |
| c++20 | MSVC/MSVC STL | 19.31 | 19.42 |
| c++23 | GCC | 16 | — |
| c++23 | Clang/libc++ | — | — |
| c++23 | MSVC/MSVC STL | — | — |

## Choosing

| situation | pick |
| --- | --- |
| new code, no constraint | GCC 15+ or Clang 20+ with libc++, `c++23` |
| Linux distribution default (GCC 13/14) | GCC 13/14, `c++23`; check `<mdspan>`/`<flat_map>` before using them |
| Apple platform | Apple Clang with libc++, `c++20` unless the deployment target ships a newer libc++ |
| Windows, MSVC toolset | VS 2022 17.14+ (19.44), `/std:c++latest`, `/Zc:__cplusplus` |
| must not upgrade the compiler | run `cpp-anything matrix features --toolchain … --version … --std …` and port only what it supports; `gate` refuses the rest |

## What the generated profile turns off

`include/cppan/profile.hpp` maps each facility cpp-anything emits to the feature-test macro the matrix knows. A port may use `CPPAN_HAS_MDSPAN`, `CPPAN_HAS_PRINT`, `CPPAN_HAS_FLAT_MAP`, `CPPAN_HAS_LIB_MODULES` and friends only when the macro is 1. `CPPAN_HAS_EXPECTED` selects `std::expected` over the `cppan::Result` fallback — the port does not have to care which.

```sh
cpp-anything matrix profile --toolchain gcc --version 13 --std c++23 > profile.hpp
```

## The matrix is data, not a promise

Every guide here is generated from cppreference's tables, with the page revision and fetch time in [README.md](README.md). If a cell disagrees with reality on your machine, the compiler wins: fix the data (`scripts/sync_matrix.py`) rather than the guide.
